newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, stability to continue.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, stability to continue.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Thursday amid marginal price fluctuations but traders said the market would remain stable with fully listed issues leading the way.
"Other stocks will follow in the footsteps of the (fully-listed) Zagrebacka banka and (drugs firm) Pliva, which are now stable," said Marijana Reskovac of Karlovacka Banka.
She said the favourable credit rating Croatia was awarded last week would further contribute to the market stability.
Six of eleven active issues rose, three fell and two were unchanged. Volume was slightly up at 19,902 units, with turnover down at 7.8 million kuna ($1.3 million).

Food processor Podravka once again took the spotlight on Thursday edging up five kuna above its nominal value to close at 305, after peaking at 310 in mid-session. It accounted for most of the trading, with 16,715 shares sold.
Reskovac said huge demand for Podravka's shares could be ascribed to the private emission of its bonds for Austrian buyers, due in the near future, which she said gives confidence to investors.
Zagrebacka Banka gained 109.90 kuna to close at 1,760, with 818 shares sold. Its GDRs trading on Seaq rose to $31.5 from Wednesday's $30.
The bank's C-series bearer shares were the gainer of the day, rising 50 kuna to 600, but sold only two units. Its preference E-series stock remained flat at 950 kuna on volume of 161 shares.
Pliva was also flat at 510 kuna with 743 units sold. Its GDRs fetched $17.185 in London by mid-afternoon, up from $17.125 a day before.
Reskovac said Zagrebacka and Pliva were poised for further growth, but at a more gradual pace.
Top decliner hotelier Arena edged down 10 kuna to 160, with 68 units sold. Hotelier Suncani Hvar was down two kuna to 161 on volume of 261 shares.
All other active hotel stocks were gainers. Istraturist added six kuna to 196, Jadranturist 20 kuna to 300 and Laguna 10 to 1,250 kuna.
Traders said new significant gains for hoteliers cannot be expected before spring.
Confectioner Kras was among decliners, down 13 kuna to 450, with 398 units changing hands. ($ = 5.810 Croatian Kuna)
